findings.summary: Brain operation policy functions do not enforce workspace tenant access.
findings.details: The new policy query/mutation accept a workspaceId but never consult workspace membership/access before returning or changing policy state, so callers reaching the Confect surface can inspect or modify another tenant workspace policy.

findings.summary: Policy updates bypass real operator authorization by hard-coding admin role.
findings.details: setPolicyInternal does not receive or load the current operator role; it always calls nextOperationPolicy with actorRole "admin", so stale or under-privileged operator behavior is only tested on the pure helper and is not enforced at the function boundary.

findings.summary: Kill-switch policy changes are not durable and produce no audit receipt.
findings.details: The implementation synthesizes default policies and returns mutation results without database writes, audit rows, receipts, or idempotency handling, so kill switches cannot reliably stop subsystems across requests/replays or satisfy rollback/audit requirements.

findings.summary: Generation fencing is ineffective because current generation is caller-derived.
findings.details: The Confect implementation constructs current.generation from input.expectedGeneration before checking it, so stale or arbitrary expectedGeneration values match by construction instead of being compared to durable state.
